key_insight: Static training graphs allow one offline solve over keep, recompute, offload and arena offsets, removing both fragmentation and coincident peak lifetimes that greedy caching allocators leave.
killer_doubt: Already published as ILPs. Remaining fragmentation is modest (GMLake measured ~15% average, up to 33% [training knowledge]); over selective recompute plus FSDP, expect ~1.2-1.5x, not 2-4x.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Sizing only: run an OLLA/MODeL-style planner on Llama-8B and 70B torch.compile graphs versus selective checkpointing with expandable segments; report peak HBM at equal step time. ~$20k GPU.
prior_art: Checkmate (MLSys'20) ILP remat; OLLA (Meta 2022) and MODeL (ICML'23) joint lifetime/offset ILP; Moccasin (ICML'23); POET (ICML'22) remat+paging; GMLake (ASPLOS'24).

key_insight: Shared system prompts, documents and few-shot blocks make prefix KV globally redundant; prefix-affinity routing stores each block once per pod and also skips its prefill compute.
killer_doubt: Shipping in production stacks. Per-pod prefix caching already captures the 30-70% shared share; cross-pod duplication left over is likely only ~1.1-1.3x more (estimate), traded against load imbalance.
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. Replay an agent-heavy multi-tenant trace through SGLang router or Dynamo with and without a global radix index; measure residual duplicate KV GB and TTFT under hotspot load. ~$15k.
prior_art: SGLang RadixAttention and cache-aware router (2024); Mooncake global KV pool (FAST'25); NVIDIA Dynamo KV-aware router; llm-d prefix-aware scheduling; Preble [training knowledge].

key_insight: GC headroom (1.5-3x live set) is DRAM bought to save CPU; one cluster-published memory-time exchange rate lets every runtime re-trade it as DRAM prices swing.
killer_doubt: MemBalancer's square-root rule cut memory ~16% at equal GC time (via search snippet); fleet gain is managed-heap share x ~16-30%, likely ~5-10% of server DRAM, with knobs already shipped.
decisive_experiment: Kubernetes pilot on ~200 JVM and Go services: map a published $/GB-hour to MemBalancer's constant via SoftMaxHeapSize/GOMEMLIMIT; compare RSS and CPU against static settings for 4 weeks, and measure fleet managed-heap share. ~$100k.
prior_art: Alonso & Appel 1990 heap 'advice server'; MemBalancer (OOPSLA'22) single tradeoff constant across heaps; US 9471225/9836394 multi-GC memory optimisation (via search snippet); Meta TMO.

key_insight: Frozen weights need only a fixed bit pattern; separating a cheap patterned film from a small sensing die is the right instinct for read-only storage economics.
killer_doubt: 200 nm pitch is 0.025 Gb/mm2, ~15x below 1b DRAM; face-to-face lamination needs silicon under all ~22,400 mm2 for 70 GB, and 20-70 ppm/K film distortion misaligns 200 nm pads.
decisive_experiment: Imprint a 1 cm2, 200 nm-pitch via crossbar with printed Schottky contacts on PET; laminate to a test die; measure overlay error across the die, rectification ratio needed at 1k x 1k, and read time. ~$300k.
prior_art: HP Labs nanoimprinted crossbar memories (mid-2000s) [training knowledge]; Taalas mask-ROM weight chips; silicon via-ROM weights dropped earlier (I-01226, I-04585, I-07639).

key_insight: Counter-based PRNG output has near-zero Kolmogorov size, so dropping and regenerating it bit-exactly on a fault (Philox >10 GB/s) beats storing or compressing it.
killer_doubt: Little such data stays resident: dropout masks are already regenerated from seeds, init tensors are overwritten after step one. Likely under 1-2% of node DRAM, not tens of GB (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Instrument 10 training and simulation jobs: sample resident pages and test whether they match a registered generator stream by regenerating and comparing. Stop if matched bytes are under 2% of DRAM. ~$20k.
prior_art: Random123 counter-based PRNGs (SC'11); FlashAttention and Megatron regenerate dropout masks from seeds; JAX stateless PRNG keys; procedural content generation [training knowledge].

key_insight: Fixed-point coupling layers invert bit-exactly, so the backward pass rebuilds each layer input with no drift and activation memory stops growing with depth.
killer_doubt: The baseline is full checkpointing at the same ~1.33x compute. Its boundary stash for a 405B model at 128k context (TP8 x CP16) is ~4 GB/GPU, under 5% of HBM.
decisive_experiment: Train a 1B integer-coupling reversible decoder and a standard Llama-1B for 20B tokens; compare loss, and peak HBM against full checkpointing plus CPU offload at 32k-128k context. ~$60k GPU.
prior_art: RevNet (2017), Reformer (2020), RevViT (CVPR'22); BDIA exact bit-level reversible transformers (2024); Maclaurin et al. 2015 exact fixed-point reversible learning [training knowledge].

key_insight: One randomized Hadamard rotation does two jobs: it flattens outliers for 3-4-bit quantization and caps the peak damage any single stored bit flip can do.
killer_doubt: Orthonormal transforms preserve error energy. At 1% BER a 4-bit code gains ~0.85 level^2 of noise, ~10x quantization noise (0.083); SNR falls ~24 to ~14 dB whatever the shape.
decisive_experiment: Fault injection into QuaRot-style INT4 weights, KV and activations at BER 1e-5 to 1e-2 with a directional retention model; measure perplexity with and without rotation. ~$15k GPU.
prior_art: Same mechanism as dropped I-08644. QuaRot, QuIP#, SpinQuant Hadamard rotations; EDEN (MICRO'19) error-tolerant DNNs on approximate DRAM.

key_insight: Per-step reseeded XOR masks turn one-way charge-loss flips into decorrelated +/-2^k errors, making quantized training stashes a natural customer for 4-level approximate DRAM (N-66).
killer_doubt: Alone it adds little: ActNN already gets ~12x with 2-bit stashes (via search snippet). At 1% BER error noise is ~10x 4-bit quantization noise; payoff needs N-66-class 2x-bit cells.
decisive_experiment: Train Llama-1B with 2-4-bit stashes under charge-loss and 4-level adjacent-drift error models at BER 1e-4 to 1e-2, masks on and off; compare loss curves. Then measure relaxed-refresh error direction on DRAM-Bender. ~$60k.
prior_art: ActNN (ICML'21) unbiased 2-bit activation compression; EDEN (MICRO'19); memory-controller data scrambling and DRAM true/anti cells [training knowledge]; Phase B N-66. Debiasing combination: none found.

key_insight: Most warm sandboxes sit idle; restoring snapshots from NVMe by lazily faulting the first invocation's working set (~5-10 ms) turns resident DRAM into cheap flash.
killer_doubt: Already shipping in Firecracker-based platforms and Lambda SnapStart. Serverless and sandbox pools are likely under 5% of fleet DRAM (estimate), so the fleet-level gain is small.
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. Size it: replay the Azure Functions and an agent-sandbox trace with REAP-style restore versus keep-warm; report DRAM GB-hours saved and p99 cold start. ~$10k.
prior_art: REAP (ASPLOS'21), FaaSnap (EuroSys'22), Firecracker snapshots, AWS Lambda SnapStart, Catalyzer (ASPLOS'20) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Token IDs are ~1e5x smaller than KV; a think-time predictor using typing and focus signals can hide KV re-creation inside the user's gap.
killer_doubt: Re-prefilling a 32k-token 70B context costs ~4.6 PFLOP (~5-9 GPU-s) per resume; NVMe restore in advanced I-08555 takes ~1-2 s with no FLOPs. Merge into I-08555.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-08555's experiment: add a re-prefill arm and report GPU-seconds per resume versus NVMe restore across 4k-128k contexts, at measured prediction hit rates. ~$10k extra.
prior_art: vLLM recompute preemption; InferCept (ICML'24); CachedAttention (ATC'24); HCache; earlier-batch I-08555 (typing-signal NVMe prefetch, advanced) and I-05417 (dropped).

key_insight: Cached documents share few distinct key-sets; storing each layout once and documents as layout ID plus packed values removes repeated keys, tags and padding.
killer_doubt: Hidden classes, key-sharing dicts and schema formats already do this; zstd with trained dictionaries compresses JSON blobs ~3-5x [training knowledge], leaving likely under 1.3x extra.
decisive_experiment: Dump a production Redis or memcached JSON cache; compare shape-sharing against zstd-dictionary and listpack on bytes per document and p99 GET latency. Stop below 1.3x over zstd-dictionary. ~$15k.
prior_art: Self maps (1989), V8 hidden classes, PyPy maps, Python PEP 412 key-sharing dicts, protobuf and Arrow schemas, Amazon Ion symbol tables [training knowledge].

key_insight: Pre-initialised golden images let thousands of instances share read-only pages copy-on-write, each holding only its private dirty pages.
killer_doubt: Android Zygote has done this since 2008; serverless forks exist. The 10-30x holds only for tiny functions; LLM-tool agent sandboxes likely dirty 20-50% of pages (estimate).
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. Measure private dirty-page fractions for 1,000 agent sandboxes (Python plus tool runtimes) forked from a golden snapshot over a full task, to size achievable density. ~$10k.
prior_art: Android Zygote; Catalyzer sfork (ASPLOS'20); SEUSS (EuroSys'20); Mitosis remote fork (OSDI'23); Firecracker snapshot clones; Lambda SnapStart [training knowledge].
